Derby, get ready for the Everett 
Blackmouth Derby March 17th and 
18th.  Tickets for the Everett Derby 
are $100 per boat and are available at 
John's Sporting Goods.  Each ticket is 
valid for up to four anglers.  There are 
only 125 tickets available for the 
Everett Derby so get those tickets 
ASAP before they run out.  Last year 
all tickets were sold a couple days 
prior to the derby.
The Everett Derby fishing area 
includes Marine Areas 8-1, 8-2 and 9.  
In the past, the Everett Derby was only 
a one-day deal.  This year the 
tournament is extended to two days 
of fishing.  First Prize is $3,000 for the 
largest Chinook weighed in. Second 
prize is $1500. Third prize is $500 and 
Fourth Prize being $250.  Also, the 
Everett Steelhead and Salmon Club 
will be hosting a Blackmouth Fishing 
Seminar at 7 PM, March 14th at 
Bayside Marine.
Winning Strategies
Do you think winning one of these two 
Chinook fishing tournaments is a roll 
of the dice or is there a bit of skill 
involved?  Last year the winner in the 
Olympic Salmon Derby was an angler 
trolling out of his sail boat at Craven 
Rock.   Not a bad pay day for a laid-
back day of salmon fishing.  However, 
most of the time these derbies are 
won by hard core salmon anglers who 
are consistently hooking up big 
Chinook salmon on a regular basis.  
Remember, you can do that!  Even if 
you have just one year of Chinook 
angling experience under the belt, I 
can make sure you are in the ballgame 
by just following a few simple rules.
Tides Do Matter
Pick out a couple of good fishing areas 
i n  a d va n c e  k n ow n  fo r  h av i n g 
productive fishing during a particular 
tide.  Don't pick an area just because 
you are comfortable fishing there. 
Honestly, you are really reducing your 
chances for success.  Hopefully you 
don't think that Chinook posted on my 
Facebook are caught because I'm a 
better salmon angler than others. 
These fish come my way because I 
have a historical sense of tide 
movement.  This takes many years of 
experience and I am more than willing 
to share these thoughts with you.
First, let's get a look at Olympic Fishing 
Derby tides.  On Saturday March 10th, 
water in Marine Areas 6 and 7 will be 
flooding by daylight and tides will be 
high at 9:17 AM.  At Mid Channel Bank 
the tide will be high around 9:45 AM.  
These are easy choices for the first day 
of the derby.  I would fish either 
Craven Rock near Port Townsend or I 
would fish the east-side of Eastern 
Bank.   A good strategy might be to 
fish Craven Rock while the tide is 
flooding and switch to fishing Mid 
Channel Bank when the tide starts to 
ebb.  This year in late February, I 
caught some decent Chinook at Mid 
Channel Bank and would have placed 
well up the ladder in any of our local 
Derby's.  By the time these salmon 
tournaments begin, there is going to 
be some early spring Chinook 
showing up at Eastern Bank and at 
Mid Channel Bank.  These salmon 
should weight in the low and middle 
teens.
The tides for the Everett Blackmouth 
Derby are certainly ideal at Mid 
Channel Bank with a 11:55 AM low at 
Port Townsend.  If you have the boat 
and desire to head to Mid Channel 
Bank on derby day, you bet it will be 
worth both time and effort. Many 
anglers are not into traveling to Mid 
Channel and that is perfectly 
acceptable since the Everett Derby 
has been won as close as Hat Island. 
Some alternatives for the Everett 
Derby are Onamac Point on Camano 
Island and Rock Point also on Camano 
Island.  Either of these Camano Island 
points are up to producing derby 
winning Chinook in March. 
Gearing Up
We can talk about spoons all day long 
but if you fish with factory hooks that 
come in the package, your chances 
are only 50/50 of landing any decent 
Chinook.  Just think losing a Chinook 
w o r t h  b e t w e e n  $ 3 , 0 0 0  a n d 
$10,000???  The best hooks and most 
expensive hooks cost just $1 each.  
Now think about this: $40 to $100 for 
a derby ticket; $50 to $100 for gas; $10 
to $25 to launch a boat; lunch; gear 
and (yes) those side bets.  You bet, 
you can afford the best hooks money 
can buy.  Believe me, the number one 
item which could put you in the prize 
money is that $1 hook.
Prior to August of last year, I was using 
Gamakatsu Big River Siwash as 
replacement hooks on my spoons.  
After a little thought, I noticed my 
hook-up to landing ratio on Chinook 
was not good.  For every two fish 
hooked-up only one fish got into the 
net.  That's not good! Things need to 
change!  I began looking for a hook 
made of thinner wire and a hook with 
a wider throat.  A little research led 
Shellfish Hotline 1-866-880-5421
me to the Owner Stinger Siwash Hook 
3/0.  The 3/0 Owner Siwash is similar 
in size to the Gamakatsu 4/0 Big River 
Siwash hook but is significantly 
sharper than the Gamakatsu Big River 
hook with a wider throat for deeper 
hook-sets.  My hook-up ratio to 
landing ratio on Chinook is now closer 
to 90%.  Now that stat did not change 
by chance!
Spoons
Recently I noticed Chinook I have 
been catching at Mid Channel Bank 
have five-inch candlefish in their 
bellies.  This makes a sound case for 
using Goldstar Coho Killer spoons 
with the Owner 3/0 Stinger Siwash 
Hook.  The top choice on Spoon colors 
should include Herring Aide and 
Cookies n Cream.
Closer to home around Possession Bar 
and Pilot Point the Chinook have a mix 
of candlefish and small herring in their 
s t o m a c h s .   I n  t h e s e  a r e a s  I 
recommend Goldstar 3.0 Kingfisher 
spoons and Coho Killer spoons each 
rigged with 3/0 Owner Stinger Siwash 
Hooks. Leader length on spoons 
should be 42 inches and tied with 
Pline 30 pound fluorocarbon leader 
material.
Fishing Depths
When I was fishing Mid Channel Bank 
in February my best fishing action 
came at 140 to 155 feet of water. I 
don't know how reliable that piece of 
fishing information might be by mid-
March, but I would keep it in mind as a 
backup plan.
Local anglers who have been fishing 
Possession Bar, Pilot Point and Point 
no Point have been catching their 
Chinook in 90 to 100 feet of water.  
Those Chinook fishing depths are 
typical for this time of year. 
No matter what depth you choose to 
fish for Chinook, just keep in mind you 
must fish close to the bottom.  If you 
don't because you are too tired or too 
cold your chances of catching a derby 
winning Chinook has now dropped 
significantly. Fishing for Chinook this 
time of year is a contact sport in every 
sense of the word.   Every few 
minutes with any change of water 
depth you should let the downrigger 
ball to the bottom and bring it back 
about five feet.  This means a great 
deal of work over a 6 to 8-hour period. 
Believe me when I tell you this, 
“Chinook anglers that are constantly 
winning and placing in the Chinook 
tournaments are checking for bottom 
every few minutes.”   You can take 
that to the bank!
I know I have told you this in the past. 
When you are out fishing, look at the 
number of anglers sitting down and 
just staring at their fishing rods.  This 
simply doesn't work. The only time 
this works is Perch fishing in Lake 
Washington.   I want you to win or 
place in one of these two Chinook 
tournaments and you will do it by 
aggressively fishing.  Now with all this 
talk about fishing, let's get out there 
and have some fun this year. Really, 
who knows what the future will hold. 
Gotta keep those hopes (and rod tips) 
high!

Information For The Serious Angler              by John Martinis                                    May 2018
John’s Sporting Goods Web Page www.johnssportinggoods.com
Puget Sound Chinook 
and Coho Seasons for 
2018
There are plenty of unconfirmed rumors 
concerning the 2018 Puget Sound salmon 
seasons swirling around the general 
fishing public.  Let me dispel the worst of 
the rumors.  Rumor (The big one): There 
will be no salmon fishing this summer. 
Really?  c'mon seriously? Yep…I get this 
question ALL THE TIME! Well now before 
you say, “Well…. I've seen this movie 
before”. Here's the answer…First, let me 
take a deep breath and tell you in no 
uncertain terms this rumor is bogus.  The 
salmon season has been greatly 
expanded compared to the 2017 salmon 
seasons. That's just the fact. Yes, there 
has been some curtailment in the 
Chinook season for some areas. However 
there has been additional Coho fishing 
days in almost all areas. If you only fish 
o n e  M a r i n e  A re a ,  yo u  m i g ht  b e 
disappointed, yet other anglers are taking 
a victory lap when they saw the new Coho 
regulations.
I will attempt to dissect the salmon fishing 
regulations for Puget Sound/San Juan's 
the best that I can, so stick with me.  
Hopefully, I can decompose these 
complexities into logical information. The 
exact dates each area opens, and closes 
could change a tad. Why? Well, there's 
reasons…since there are Chinook quotas 
to deal with that could end a season 
earlier than expected. So, right now it's 
not a sure thing.
Disclaimer: These salmon fishing dates, 
limits and seasons may change.  So, let's 
begin.
This column is based on information that 
was available April 29, 2018.  If you see 
something I missed or needs corrected 
send me an “Oops!” email and I will send 
out a correction on Facebook.
Just in case you're wondering the seasons 
being outlined are summer seasons, I will 
look at the winter/spring seasons later in 
the year.
Tulalip Bubble:  Opens May 25th for 
hatchery or wild Chinook.  Open every 
week Friday, Saturday, Sunday and until 
noon on Monday.  Closes September 4th.  
You can fish with two rods in this area if 
you have the two rod endorsement.
Marine Area 7:  Opens July 1st, for 
hatchery Chinook only. This part of the 
Chinook season goes through July 31st.  
On August 1st you can keep hatchery or 
wild Chinook through September 3rd 
(Labor Day). Yep, sure can. Area 7 will be 
o p e n  fo r  C o h o  J u l y  1 st  t h ro u g h 
September 30th. Hatchery or wild Coho 
can be kept. Yes. Yes, it does mean clipped 
and unclipped. Last year Area 7 was 
completely closed for Coho fishing.
Marine Areas 8-1 and 8-2: The Chinook 
season for these two Marine areas start 
December 1st and end April 30, 2019.  
Marine Areas 8-1 and 8-2 Coho:  Now the 
good news: Coho fishing will start August 
1st and end on September 30th.  That is 
60 more days of Coho fishing than the 
2017 season when there wasn't any Coho 
fishing in Areas 8-1 or 8-2.  You will be

able to keep hatchery or wild Coho in

Marine Area 9: Chinook fishing starts 
on July 16th and is scheduled through 
August 15th.  …BUT!!  This season is 
based on a quota of 5,563 hatchery 
Chinook.  Only clipped adipose fin 
(hatchery Chinook) can be kept.
Area 9 Coho: July 16th through 
September 30th, hatchery Coho only. 
Only clipped adipose fin (hatchery 
Coho) can be kept.
Marine Area 10:  Although Area 10 
opens for Coho on June 1st, you must 
release Chinook. You can keep hatchery 
Chinook starting July 16th through 
August 30th.  The Chinook quota for 
Area 10 is 4,743, up significantly from 
2017.  This season could close before 
August 30th, if the Chinook quota is 
met. 
Area 10 Coho:  June 1st to November 
15th.  Hatchery and wild Coho can be 
kept.  In the 2017 Area 10 Coho season 
only hatchery Coho could be kept. 
As you can see Coho fishing has a 
completely different look in 2018 
versus 2017.  If you add up the 
combined fishing days of all the Puget 
Sound/San Juan fishing areas, more 
than 200 days of Coho fishing are 
available in the 2018 that were not 
available in 2017. That seems very, very 
clear.  The Chinook quota in Area 10 has 
been significantly increased.  The 
Chinook quota in Marine Area 9 is 
roughly the same as last year and the 
summer Chinook fishing days are the 
same as last year. Now does that sound 
to you like salmon fishing will not be 
open? I know we're dealing in a world of 
sentiment and we must resist those 
reflexive impulses. We need to show 
some (very) cautious optimism.
Baker Lake Sockeye: The forecast for 
sockeye returning to Baker Lake is 
strong enough to allow for a lake 
fishery, open July 7th through early 
September and a fishery on the Skagit 
River, which is open June 16th to July 
15th for sockeye fishing.
Puget Sound 
Halibut Fishing
In the April Newsletter, I wrote about 
rigging for Halibut fishing.  Now let's 
explore some places to go Halibut 
fishing in Puget Sound. The two main 
areas to fish for Halibut in Puget Sound 
are Mutiny Bay and Admiralty Bay.  
Mutiny Bay is the closest place to fish 
for Halibut in Puget Sound and it is not 
too far from three popular boat 
launches: Everett, Edmonds and 
Shilshole. When fishing Mutiny Bay, 
there is no reason to be concerned 
about how big the tide is or if the tide is 
high or low.  Go to Mutiny and plan on 
spending an eight hour day fishing to 
have a reasonable chance of catching a 
Halibut.
There two ways that you can fish in 
Mutiny Bay or anywhere else, either 
drifting or on anchor.  If you do not want 
to mess around with an anchor you can 
drift across the Bay in 90 to 150 feet of 
water using a spreader bar and squid rig 
with a whole herring attached.  If you 
did not see my Halibut video in the April 
Newsletter here is the link to that video, 
click here for video.    As you are drifting 
across the Bay occasionally bounce the 
Halibut rig on the bottom.  There is not 
one place that is better fishing in 
Mutiny it is just a matter of covering lots 
of water in search of fish. 
When anchoring for Halibut there are 
different options available for catching 
Halibut.  In recent years when I have 
been on anchor in search of Halibut I 
have been fishing off of my downrigger.  
In this situation I rig a 7 to 9-inch white 
squid with a 7 to 8-inch herring tied 
inside the squid.  Let this rig out 25 feet 
behind the boat and attach the line to a 
downrigger release and let the rig to the 
bottom.  Bring the downrigger ball up 
one foot from the bottom.  The 
downrigger release should be two feet 
above the lead ball.  This will work well 
until the tide slows to a crawl.  When 
the tide approaches slack tide put on a 
spreader bar and squid and do not use 
the downrigger again until the tides 
starts moving.  If you attempt to fish 
with the downrigger during slack tide 
the gear becomes tangled.  The water 
near the bottom gets turbulent during 
slack tide and tangles the gear.
Admiralty Bay can be accessed from all 
boat launches I mentioned plus the Fort 
Casey boat launch on Whidbey Island.  
If you have a small boat this is a good 
place to get access to the water and not 
have to be very far from the boat 
launch.  Fishing at Admiralty Bay for 
Halibut is exactly like fishing Mutiny 
Bay.
Puget Sound Halibut Maps
Mutiny Bay
Admiralty Bay
If you want to fish in Area 6 or Area 7 for 
Halibut I recommend three places: 
Partridge Bank, Eastern Bank and Hein  
Bank
Partridge Bank:   The largest Halibut 
that I caught in Washington came from 
the north end of Partridge bank in 60 
feet of water.  This is a good spot to 
anchor or drift for Halibut.  I also like 
the southwest corner of Partridge 
Shellfish Hotline 1-866-880-5421
Bank.  I regularly catch Halibut when I 
am salmon fishing in March and April 
on the southwest corner of Partridge 
Bank.   If you want to anchor in this 
area you might want to look at the 
tides on the day you are going Halibut 
fishing.  There is a considerable 
amount of tidal movement on the 
south end of Partridge bank.  If the tide 
is moving too swiftly, you can drift fish 
in this area and anchor when the water 
slows down.  Partridge Bank Halibut 
fishing can be good in 60 to 150 feet of 
water.
Eastern Bank: The southwest corner of 
Eastern Bank is the best location for 
Halibut fishing.  I would recommend 
fishing in 90 to 125 feet of water
Hein Bank: Hein Bank has many good 
areas to fish.  My favorite area is the 
northeast corner of the Bank.  The 
extreme southern end of the Bank is 
also a good area for Halibut.  You can 
fish either location in 90 to 150 feet of 
water.
On any of these Banks, I prefer to 
anchor versus drifting for Halibut since 
it is much easier to let the fish swim to 
you.  However anchoring in the Straits 
of Juan de Fuca is not for everyone.  
Those of you who prefer to drift will do 
just fine.  I would also recommend 
trolling for Halibut.  Trolling for Halibut 
with a downrigger is very effective.  
Troll a 7 to 8-inch whole Herring slowly 
just as you would for salmon.  
Remember I catch Halibut regularly on 
spoons when I am trolling for salmon 
on Partridge Bank.  It works!

Partridge Bank
Eastern Bank
Hein Bank

Puget Sound Lingcod 
Fishing Areas 
Opens May 1st: Most of the bottom in 
Puget Sound is made up of mud and 
silt.  Not an ideal habitat for Lingcod. 
The rocky areas of Puget Sound, 
whether it is a jetty or a rocky bottom, 
is where you will find Lingcod.  Let's 
take a look at some of those areas.
The Possession Bar area in Puget 
Sound is the best location to fish for 
Lingcod.  There is a good population of 
Lings that live on Possession Bar all 
year.  Then there are transient Lings 
that visit Possession Bar this time of 
year.  Many of you have experienced 
catching Lingcod while fishing for 
salmon on the west side of the Bar.  
Makes you wonder how accidently 
catching these critters is easier than 
catching them when the Lingcod 
season is open?
Most of the Lingcod on Possession Bar 
can be found in 45 to 65 feet of water.  
Some of these areas are rocky and 
some of the areas are indents in the 
bar.  Near the Scatchet Head Buoy 
there is a huge rock pile that holds a 
pretty large population of Lingcod.  
This is easy to find since it is a popular 
area to fish and it will be well marked 
by others that are fishing for Lingcod.  I 
usually choose to fish for Lingcod 
across the face of Possession Bar in 60 
to 65 feet of water.  I am looking for 
slight elevations or slight depressions 
in the Bar.  These slight depth changes 
are usually where Lingcod hang out 
looking to ambush some small fish or 
Octopus. 
The jetty's around the Edmonds 
Marina and around Shilshole Marina 
are good places to catch Lingcod.  
These places are only good for a couple 
of days because they get fished out 
rather quickly after the May 1st 
opening day.  In these two areas cast 2 
ounce lead heads rigged with 4 inch 
twin tail motor oil scampi tails into the 
rocks and keep the jig moving so that it 
does not get hooked up in the rocks.
Scampi Tails
4-inch Motor Oil Scampi Tail
Drift fishing with a live sand sole is an 
effective method.  You can catch these 
sand sole along the beach from the 
Clinton Ferry on Whidbey Island to 
Possession Bar.  These sole can be 
caught in 60 to 100 feet of water.  Use a 
Gamakatsu top and Bottom Rig to 
catch the sole with a small piece of 
squid for bait.  Keep the sand sole alive 
in a bucket of water and regularly 
change the water. 
Tackle
Gamakatsu Top and Bottom Rig
Lingcod Hooks
Now as for the future of angling in 
Puget Sound… Who knows, indeed. 
This is one thing that seems very, very 
clear. We can all become agents for 
change. Typically, when we all push for 
the same agenda good things happen.

maps.title: Edmonds Area 10 Coho
maps.text:
Fishing Maps
Maps For The Serious Angler                                     By John Martinis                                        
January Feb     March   April      May     June      July     August   Sept        Oct        Nov        Dec
Edmonds/Area 10 Coho
Coho Coho Coho
John’
s Sporting Goods
Here is how I would fish the oil docks at 
Edmonds.  Start fishing at the south end of 
the oil docks in 200 feet of water.  I would 
wander around to locate huge schools of bait.  
Once I locate the bait, I will try to stay on top 
of the bait or stay in a depth range where the 
bait is located.  I would troll south to the 
weather buoy near Richmond Beach.  If 
there are rip lines on the water I would troll 
parallel to the rip lines unless the bait schools 
made a compelling case to troll somewhere 
else.  If there is not too much tidal movement 
I would troll back to the oil docks once I got 
to the weather buoy.  If there are a series of 
larger tides sometimes it makes sense to pull 
the gear and run in a direction so that you can 
troll a long distance in the same direction that 
the tide is moving.  The tidal movement in 
the Richmond Beach area is somewhat 
subdued making it easy to troll in either 
direction.
When Coho fishing in Marine Area 10 I like to 
start fish in 120 feet of water right off Edwards 
Point and half way to the oil docks.  For the 
first hour of fishing I will concentrate on 
fishing between 120 and 220 feet of water.  
Some mornings this area is almost impossible 
to fish because the sea weed and eel grass gets 
so thick in these areas that I will have to move 
out to deeper cleaner water.
By 7AM I will start fishing depths that will 
range from 160 to 300 feet and I will regularly 
go back to check what is going on at 160 feet 
or even at 120 feet.  By 8AM I will fish depths 
that will range from 300 feet to 700 feet.  
Oil Dock
Edmonds

maps.text:
Fishing Maps
Maps For The Serious Angler                                        
January Feb     March   April      May     June      July     August   Sept        Oct        Nov        Dec
Elliot Bay Chinook
Chinook
3
The prime trolling area, Gary Krein (All Star 
Charters) says, is a sort of "J" shape, running 
from Duwamish Head south, across the 
Duwamish Waterway and the industrial dock 
area, and up the east (Seattle) side to about the 
ferry terminal.  The really prime part of that 
area is right in front of the Duwamish 
Waterway, and into the Waterway a short 
distance.
"The bulk of the kings in this fishery are 
probably caught 30 to 60 feet deep, and maybe 
as far down as 90 if the traffic is heavy," Krein 
says.  "They do feed at times, so watch your 
sounder and if you happen to see a 
concentration of bait, it's worthwhile to go 
down and fish it."

There are two places the Hood Canal Coho 
fishery takes place: just south of the Hood Canal 
Bridge and in Dabob Bay.  The fishing is very 
similar to anywhere else in Puget Sound.  The 
fishing is done in deep water for suspended 
Coho.  Troll until around until you find schools

Fishing for Chinook at Kingston/Apple Tree Point can take 
on a different look in the Summer Chinook fishing season 
as opposed to the Winter Chinook fishing season.  In the 
Winter season, I like following the contour of the bar in 90-
120 feet of water.  In the Summer Chinook season, fishing 
can be good along the contour of the bar as well as out in 
much deeper water.  The location of the Chinook in the 
Summer all depends on the location of the bait.  
Sometimes the bait will get parked out in 140-180 feet of 
water and at other times the bait will hug the bar.  Every 
year the bait will present itself at varying depths.
Rigs to use: Gibbs red racer flasher with a Silver Horde #340 
Chartreuse Ace Hi fly rigged 36” behind the flasher or a 
Gibbs red racer flasher with a Goldstar 3.5 #964 Kingfisher 
spoon rigged 42” behind the flasher.  Use 30lb Pline 
fluorocarbon leader material to tie both rigs.

Tin Shed Drift
The Tin Shed Drift is approximately contained in the 
blue oval that is outlined on the map.  The best 
Chinook fishing in this area can be either when the tide 
is going out or when the tide is coming in.  I prefer to 
fish in this area when the tide is going out.  Most of the 
time (not always) the fish will be suspended on the 
edge of Possession Bar in this area.  The edge of the 
Bar in this area is very steep.  When the tide is going 
out, the tide pushes the bait and the salmon up against 
this steep edge.
Gear that I would recommend: Gibbs Red Racer 
Flasher  with a Goldstar 3.0 or 3.5 Kingfisher spoon 42 
inches behind the flasher. Spoon colors that I 
recommend are #395 (Herring Aide)  and 964 (Green 
Spatter/Red Stripe).  During the summer Chinook 
season I would recommend using 5" Tomic Plugs in 
colors 602 and 603.

Open Bay Chinook
ChinookChinook Chinook
Fish open Bay when the tide is coming in.  Follow the 
90-120 contour line from San Juan Island to Henry 
Island.  The bottom is smooth and easy to navigate.  
After the tide is high and the water starts going out, head 
for Pile Point or Eagle Point on the west side of San 
Juan Island.
Rigs to use: Whole Herring, Gibbs Red Racer flasher 
with a Goldstar Herring Aide Coho Killer 42” behind

maps.title: Pile Point/Eagle Point Map
maps.text:
Pile Point/Eagle Point 
Fish at Pile Point when the tide 
is going out.  No need to fish 
close to the bottom at this spot 
because the Chinook will be 
suspended.  Fish for Chinook 
here at 60 to 90 feet.  The depth 
can be anywhere from 90-250 
feet. 
San Juan Island 
You can fish at Eagle Point close to the bottom or 
you can fish for suspended Chinook.  If you are 
fishing the bottom, keep your downriggers 
between 90-120 feet and close to the bottom.  You 
can fish for suspended Chinook between 60 and 
90 feet deep.  If you are fishing for suspended 
Chinook, troll along the rips.  Fish at Eagle on 
either tide, however the outgoing tide is often the 
best fishing.

be fished on either tide.  If the tide is ebbing 
(going out) start fishing approximately one 
mile south of Edwards Point and troll towards 
Edwards Point.  If the tide is flooding I would 
start trolling at Edwards Point and troll 
approximately one mile south.  My 
recommendation would be to troll in only one 
direction depending on which way the water 
was moving. I would fish in 90-120 feet of 
water.
Tackle that I would recommend 
for Richmond Chinook: Gibbs 
Red Racer flasher, Coho Killer 
spoon #395 Herring Aide, Coho 
Killer Spoon #675 Cookies n 
Cream and 3.5 Kingfisher 
spoon #395 Herring Aide.  
There is a good chance that 
Sand Lance and Herring will be 
present at Richmond Beach so 
be prepared to use larger 
spoons.

maps.title: Rigging Anchovies
maps.text:
Rigging Anchovies
John’s Sporting Goods
Tie two 2/0 black Gamakatsu hook in tandem with 30lb leader material.  Notice how close they are 
tied together.  Place Anchovy in Anchovy head holder.  Insert red pin through the holder to pin the 
Anchovy to the head holder.
Insert the front hook into the Anchovy along the lateral line.  Notice that the eye of the hook is very 
close to the back end of the holder.  This is very important so that the Anchovy does not get too much 
of a bend.  Now pull the leader through the holder so that the Anchovy gets the slightest bend to it.  
The bend in the Anchovy will be very subtle. 
Materials Needed: 30lb Leader, Rhys Davis Anchovy Heads, Gamakatsu 2/0-4/0 Hooks.  Colors of 
Anchovy heads should be Clear UV or Army Truck.  This Illustration is using 5 inch Anchovies, use 
larger hooks with 6-6.5 inch Anchovies. This rig can be used with or without a flasher.  Without a 
flasher, the leader should be 6-9 feet long.  The leader should be 60 inches if you are going to use a 
flasher.

maps.title: Shrimp Bait Formula
maps.text:
Shrimp Bait Formula 
by John Martinis-John’s Sporting Goods 
 
 
 
Items needed:  
Friskies Ocean White Fish w/ Tuna canned cat food 
Bumble Bee canned Mackerel 
Super Bait Prawn Bait pellets 
Pro Cure Shrimp Attractant Oil 
6” bait barrel  
 
The idea of mixing all these ingredients together is to set up a scent trail to attract shrimp 
to your shrimp pot.  Once the shrimp are near your pot, there is a good chance that they 
will want to enter the pot and feed on the Mackerel and pellets.  The cat food and the Pro 
Cure shrimp oil will quickly leach out of the pot and attract shrimp.  The pellets and the 
Mackerel will keep the shrimp in the pot once they get inside.  You can see the purpose 
of the different ingredients.   
 
Some people like to mix all the ingredients together and freeze the mixture in a large bait 
barrel.  They put the frozen mixture in the pot and let it un-thaw while the pot is working.  
Some people will add ground up fish to the mixture and others will add dry cat food 
(Friskies Seafood Sensation). 
 
My recommendation per pot:  
1) Put 3 cups of Super Bait shrimp bait pellets in a zip lock bag and add 1 cup of Pro 
Cure shrimp Attractant Oil in the zip lock bag.  Soak the pellets for one hour 
before shrimping. 
2) After the pellets soak for one hour, put the pellets in the 6” bait barrel.  Hang the 
bait barrel from the inside of the shrimp pot. 
3) Poke holes in one can of Mackerel and insert the can in the center bait 
compartment in the shrimp pot. 
4) Poke holes in 2 cans of Friskies Ocean White Fish w/ Tuna and insert the cans in 
the center bait compartment in the shrimp pot 
5)  Lets the shrimp pot over board and soak the pot for 45-60 minutes. 
 
Each time you let the shrimp pot out and retrieve it, you need to replace the canned cat 
food.  It pretty much washes out of the cans fairly fast.  The pellets will last all day and 
the canned Mackerel will last most of day.  The cat food is the only item that needs 
frequent replacing. 
 
I have recommended this concoction to many shrimp anglers and they find that it works 
quite well.  Some anglers will just use the pellets; other anglers will use only the canned 
Mackerel.  Use it all to set up that good scent trail. 
 
Click here for shrimp gear and bait 
 
John’s Sporting Goods
